concepts.title: Siri AI assistant
concepts.canonicalSummary: A rebuilt voice and text assistant that holds multi-turn conversations, draws on the user's own on-device information, acts inside applications, answers general knowledge questions from the web, and is reachable through a dedicated app whose history follows the user across their devices.

citations.locator: Section 1 heading: Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and an Entirely New Siri Experience
citations.supports: The vendor's own definition of the assistant, its personal-context and cross-app scope, and the dedicated app with iCloud-synced history.

concepts.title: Siri AI developer-testing availability by platform
concepts.canonicalSummary: The staged arrival of the rebuilt assistant in developer prerelease builds, where some platforms receive it at the first seed of a cycle and at least one platform is explicitly deferred to a later seed.

citations.locator: Availability > bullet beginning with the Siri AI developer-testing statement
citations.supports: That the assistant reached developer testing on four platforms at the first seed while watchOS was deferred to a later seed of the same cycle.
citations.shortQuote: Siri AI will be available for developer testing in a future watchOS 27 beta.

concepts.title: Stricter transport security for system management processes
concepts.canonicalSummary: Selected operating-system processes that handle device management, enrollment, configuration profiles, application installation and software updates begin refusing servers that do not meet a raised minimum transport-security bar.

citations.locator: Network Security > New Features
citations.supports: The affected process categories and the raised transport-security floor, stated as beginning with the 27 releases.

concepts.title: Localized asset packs for on-demand app content
concepts.canonicalSummary: Applications can ship downloadable content split by language so the system delivers only the variants matching a user's language preferences, reducing the storage an installed app consumes.

citations.locator: Background Assets > New Features
citations.supports: That localized asset packs exist and that selection follows the user's preferred languages.

concepts.title: On Demand Resources deprecated in favour of Background Assets
concepts.canonicalSummary: The older mechanism for fetching app resources on demand, together with its request API, is marked deprecated and developers are directed to the newer asset-delivery framework instead.

citations.locator: On Demand Resources > Deprecations
citations.supports: The deprecation and the named replacement framework.

concepts.title: Commerce API support for volume purchases and subscription bundles
concepts.canonicalSummary: The in-app commerce framework gains transaction states describing centrally assigned and revoked licences, product types describing bundled and grouped subscriptions, and partner identification fields on transaction and renewal records.

citations.locator: StoreKit > New Features
citations.supports: The assigned-ownership and assignment-revoked states, the bundle and suite product types, and the partner identification fields.

concepts.title: Asynchronous document protocols replace the older file-document protocol
concepts.canonicalSummary: The declarative UI framework introduces separate readable and writable document protocols supporting asynchronous access, progress reporting and direct file access, combines them into a single protocol, and deprecates the earlier file-document protocol.

citations.locator: SwiftUI > New Features and SwiftUI > Deprecations
citations.supports: The new asynchronous document protocols, the combined protocol, and the deprecation of the earlier protocol.

concepts.title: Scene-based application lifecycle becomes mandatory
concepts.canonicalSummary: Applications compiled against the current system SDK must adopt the scene-based lifecycle model; those that do not will fail to launch.

citations.locator: UIKit > Deprecations
citations.supports: That adoption is mandatory for apps built with the latest SDK and that non-adopting apps fail to launch.

concepts.title: DiskImageKit disk-image framework
concepts.canonicalSummary: A framework exposing native Swift interfaces for creating and managing disk images in a sparse image format and in raw form, intended for attachment to virtual machines.

citations.locator: Disk Images > New Features
citations.supports: The framework's existence, its supported image formats, and its intended use with the virtualization framework.

concepts.title: Wind-down of Intel translation support on macOS
concepts.canonicalSummary: The Intel translation layer is no longer reinstated automatically after upgrading, applications previously forced through translation now launch natively, installer defaults shift to the native architecture, the system surfaces Intel software that will not run on the following major release, and all Intel software except legacy games is stated to be incompatible with that following release.

citations.locator: Rosetta > New Features and Rosetta > Deprecations
citations.supports: Native launching of previously translated apps, non-restoration of the translation layer after upgrade, installer architecture defaults, plug-in auditing guidance, and the stated incompatibility of Intel software with the next major release except legacy games.

citations.locator: EcosystemUI > New Features
citations.supports: That the system settings interface lists Intel applications incompatible with the next major release and identifies unused Intel software.

concepts.title: DVD playback framework withdrawn from the SDK
concepts.canonicalSummary: The legacy optical-disc playback framework is removed from the development kit so applications can no longer build against it, with full removal from the operating system stated for a later release.

citations.locator: DVDPlayback > Deprecations
citations.supports: Removal from the SDK, the inability to build against it, and the stated future removal.

concepts.title: Reduced-security startup mode blocked installation of the first seed
concepts.canonicalSummary: Machines configured for a relaxed startup security policy could not install the cycle's first developer seed; the condition is later recorded as resolved.

citations.locator: Software Update > Resolved Issues > entry naming Reduced Security mode and macOS 27 beta 1
citations.supports: That the installation failure was scoped specifically to the first beta and that it was subsequently resolved.

concepts.title: Activating the assistant by looking at its orb
concepts.canonicalSummary: On the spatial platform the assistant can be started by directing one's gaze at the assistant's on-screen orb and speaking, as an alternative to the spoken wake phrase.

citations.locator: Siri > New Features > gaze activation entry, which states it was enabled in Beta 2
citations.supports: The interaction itself and, critically, the specific beta at which it became active.

concepts.title: Mesh compression incompatibility across an early seed boundary
concepts.canonicalSummary: Compressed geometry produced for one early prerelease seed is not interoperable with the following seed, so assets must be regenerated when moving across that boundary.

citations.locator: USDKit > Deprecations > mesh compression entry naming Beta 1 and Beta 2
citations.supports: The incompatibility and the exact pair of seeds it sits between.

concepts.title: Carrier calling regression on a watch prerelease seed
concepts.canonicalSummary: On one named carrier, cellular calling and emergency text messaging failed on watches that had been upgraded to, or cleanly installed with, a specific prerelease seed; the condition is later recorded as resolved.

citations.locator: Cellular > Resolved Issues > entry naming the carrier and watchOS 27.0 beta 2
citations.supports: The failure, the carrier scope, the seed it was introduced on, and its later resolution.

concepts.title: Headphone firmware updating restored during prerelease
concepts.canonicalSummary: A pair of over-ear headphones could not receive firmware updates on the earliest prerelease seeds of the cycle; the capability is recorded as available from a named later seed.

citations.locator: AirPods Max 2 > Resolved Issues > entry stating the failure applied to betas prior to Beta 2
citations.supports: That the limitation was scoped to seeds before the second beta.

concepts.title: Heart rate and cycling power training zones in the health store
concepts.canonicalSummary: The health data framework gains representations for heart rate zones and cycling power zones, letting applications read and reason about training intensity bands.

citations.locator: HealthKit > New Features
citations.supports: The addition of heart rate and cycling power zones.

concepts.title: Public beta channel opens for a release cycle
concepts.canonicalSummary: A prerelease that has been limited to enrolled developers is made available to the general public beta programme, widening who can install it without necessarily changing the software payload.

citations.locator: Availability > first bullet, naming the public beta programme and the following month

citations.locator: Opening paragraphs and the sentence stating the public beta matches the third developer beta

concepts.title: Automatic preloading of upcoming episodes in the television app
concepts.canonicalSummary: The television application can download the next episodes of a series a viewer is part-way through, and remove them once watched, so playback continues without waiting on a network.

citations.locator: Numbered change list, the television app automatic download entry
citations.supports: The toggle, the two-episode lookahead, and the deletion of watched downloads.

citations.locator: Numbered change list, the television app episode download entry
citations.supports: Independent confirmation that the app downloads upcoming episodes as the viewer progresses.

concepts.title: Zooming photographs to fill a near-matching screen
concepts.canonicalSummary: A photo library setting slightly enlarges images whose proportions almost match the display so they fill the screen rather than showing thin borders.

citations.locator: Numbered change list, the Photos zoom setting entry

citations.locator: Numbered change list, the Photos zoom setting entry

concepts.canonicalSummary: The assistant's voice picker is reworked with additional voices and pacing and expressivity controls, and a separate setting governs how many lines of a conversation are previewed in the assistant's history list.

qualityChecks.reviewNotes: Status is deliberately needsEvidenceReview, not readyForEditorialReview; only an independent evidence reviewer or the coordinator may raise it. Two gates warrant a reviewer's attention. First, rawHashesReproduced is false by design: no raw page snapshots were retained, so raw fields are null throughout and only selected-text paths, byte counts and SHA-256 values exist. Second, undocumentedClaimsMeetHigherEvidenceBar is true only because single-sourced undocumented observations were deliberately kept as claims rather than promoted to occurrences. Three such items were demoted this way: the Notification Centre wallpaper animation on the iOS public beta and beta 4 targets, the assistant transcription accessibility setting, and the disputed watch device-scope statement. Every occurrence marked corroborated has two genuinely independent sources; sources declared non-independent in their lineage notes, namely the release feed against the release index, the two same-author articles of 22 June, and the two same-author articles of 13 July, were never counted twice. The maximum unquoted overlap with source text in reader-facing fields is five normalised words, occurring only in proper nouns and API identifiers such as framework and type names, which cannot be paraphrased without losing accuracy. One deliberate short quotation of fourteen words appears, on the watch beta 1 assistant deferral occurrence, and is attributed to the vendor announcement. Verbatim vendor footnote text is retained only in the ignored evidence directory and is not reproduced in this packet.
qualityChecks.evidenceReviewNotes: Independent adversarial review by evidence-reviewer-os27-cycle, who did not author this packet. All thirteen delivery gates in docs/research-agent-handoff.md pass. Verified independently: exact 18/18 target closure with zero identity drift against assignment.json; 215 local IDs unique with no cross-namespace collision; all 257 citations resolve to declared sources, every claim and occurrence carries at least one citation, and no citation has a weak locator; all 28 declared sources are used. All 28 selected-text SHA-256 hashes and byte counts were recomputed and reproduce exactly (28/28), well beyond the 8 required. No source declares a raw capture anywhere, which is consistent with rawHashesReproduced being false; batch-gap-capture-method is a genuine and candid disclosure, not a cover for sloppy handling, and it states the correct consequence, that locators resolve against the retained extracts rather than live page markup. The extracts are structured, provenance-headed condensations of the cited documents, not fabrications: the release-notes extracts preserve framework sections in document order, and marked verbatim blocks are retained only in the ignored evidence directory. Locators were spot-checked well past the required minimum across all six platforms and every one resolved, including the framework headings on iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS and visionOS, the mid-cycle journalism locators, and the build-listing rows. The packet claim that exactly nine entries across the batch name a specific beta reproduces exactly (1 iOS/iPadOS, 0 tvOS, 2 macOS, 3 visionOS, 3 watchOS).
